subject: Network failure modes, operator checklist & attack scenarios
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <security@halcyon.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Halcyon RFP: failure modes and operator controls (initial request)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking our call last week. As part of Halcyon Financial's internal RFP for LLM inference vendors we need a short packet that explains:

- How Redwood identifies and mitigates multi-tenant network failure modes (eg. sidecar fail-open, routing table misconfigs, overlay partitioning).
- An operator checklist that our SREs can use during onboarding and periodic audits.
- A short attack-scenarios summary showing plausible lateral movement paths and compensating controls.

Can you provide an evidence packet we can attach to the questionnaire by EOD Thursday? If possible include a diagram and a one-page operator checklist.

Thanks,
Alex Mercer
Security Architect, Halcyon Financial
security@halcyon.com

Attachment: halcyon-questionnaire.pdf (referenced)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <security@halcyon.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Halcyon RFP: failure modes and operator controls (initial request)

Alex —

Appreciate the clear ask. I've attached a brief packet that covers the three items and included a failure-mode diagram. Highlights in the packet:

- We classify failure modes into Control Plane (CP), Data Plane (DP), and Sidecar/Proxy (SC). Each class has a mapped detection signal (telemetry) and automatic mitigation policy.
- For sidecar fail-open we use a two-stage guard: a local process supervisor that marks the instance unhealthy plus a dataplane egress policy that defaults to block for tenant traffic unless explicit connectivity is observed.
- KV cache poisoning is mitigated by per-tenant cache namespaces, signed K/V metadata, and a TTL + LRU eviction profile tuned by workload.
- Operator checklist (page 3) contains 12 discrete verification steps for onboarding and quarterly audits.

I've attached three artifacts: operator-checklist.pdf, failure-mode-diagram.vsdx, and kv-cache-evidence.txt (sample telemetry snippets). Please confirm this format meets your auditor's needs or call out any extra evidence they want.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer — Security
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachments: operator-checklist.pdf (11 KB), failure-mode-diagram.vsdx (150 KB), kv-cache-evidence.txt (6 KB)

Subject: Internal: quick clarifications before sending to Halcyon

Kimberly / Vanessa —

Thanks for pulling the packet together. A couple of clarifications Halcyon's team will likely ask for, can we add short bullets for each?

1) Network partition detection: which specific metrics/alerts should be shown to auditors (e.g., sustained flow drop to <x%, sidecar-health flapping >3x within 5m).
2) Sidecar mitigation timeline: how long before autoscaler marks the instance unhealthy vs operator action?
3) Proof of isolation: can we include a sanitized audit trace showing a tenant traffic flow being dropped by egress policy? (we can sanitize AZ IDs)

If we can add 2–3 lines under each section in the packet I think this avoids a follow-up. I can take 1) and 3) if Vanessa wants to author 2).

Jonas
Principal Product Security Engineer
jonas_weber@redwood.com

Alex —

Per Jonas' note I added two small clarifying pages to the packet and attached the sanitized trace you requested. Summary of changes included at the top of the packet:

- Network partition detection: recommended auditor signals are sustained flow drop >40% for >=2 minutes, sidecar-health flapping threshold (3 failures in 5m), and control-plane API latency >300ms for 3 consecutive samples.
- Sidecar mitigation timeline: supervisor marks sidecar instance UNHEALTHY within 20s of liveness failure. Autoscaler usually removes the instance within 2–3 minutes depending on policy; routes are marked unhealthy to avoid forwarding during that interval.
- Proof of isolation: attached trace (kv-cache-evidence.txt) shows a tenant flow that attempted egress to an unexpected IP and was dropped by the egress filter; all identifiers redacted.

If Halcyon's auditors want a short recorded walkthrough we can schedule a 30-minute screen-share (I can join with Jonas). Otherwise the packet should be fine for the RFP upload.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer — Security
Redwood Inference
